doc.title: Professor Longhair (Henry Roeland Byrd) Interview, 1978-Fall Transcript

title: Mardi Gras Indians rehearsing at his house
summary: He rehearsed alongside the Wild Magnolias and Wild Tchoupitoulas; SPEAKER_03 explains the tribes' split.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Were you ever associated with any of the Indian tribes, or the Mardi Gras Indian tribes? Here in New Orleans or other places?

Well, I know, uh, Wild Chapitulas, and, uh, Wild Magnolias, and really, we all have rehearsals together. I mean, the Wild Magnolias, we've rehearsed in the same building, from 70 up until about 73, the Indian tribes.
Mm-hmm. And Fess used to let them use his house and his piano for rehearsals when they were preparing for the album. And so they got to know him pretty well. They all live in the same neighborhood.
You're in the Wild Magnolias neighborhood? Yeah. Are they working on a new album?

No, they've split up. Okay, I didn't know. The Wild Chapitulas, I guess, have possibly got another album underway. The Magnolias, uh, as they were, don't exist anymore. It's now separated into two tribes.
Went to, are you saying that some of the Magnolias went?

Some of the Magnolias went one way, and the Golden Eagles, who were always part of the Wild Magnolias. It was a misnomer to begin with because it was always the Golden Eagles and the Wild Magnolias, and it just sounded more romantic, to use one name.
